metadata.description: Hand-verified gold set of ~50 OpenI chest X-ray studies for gate G1 (critical-finding recall == 1.0): medscope.critical.triage() must not miss any case whose expected_critical is non-empty. Built by running scripts/build_critical_goldset.py against the local /tmp/openi_probe probe slice (3955 reports, 108 locally-available images) to propose candidates, then manually reading each candidate's FINDINGS/IMPRESSION text and cross-checking MeSH terms (human-assigned, independent of the free-text negation the candidate script is trying to parse) before it was allowed into this file. See scripts/build_critical_goldset.py's module docstring for the negation-heuristic methodology and its known limitations.

Pneumothorax.note: Well represented: 15 confirmed positives spanning small (3.3mm-1cm), moderate (3.2-3.3cm), and large/complete pneumothoraces, including hydro- and hemopneumothorax variants (14 pure-pneumothorax cases plus study 895, which is also the single Pneumomediastinum-positive case below). Positive regardless of size -- unlike PleuralEffusion, pneumothorax criticality is not severity-gated in this ontology.

PleuralEffusion.note: 14 confirmed LARGE-effusion positives (explicitly graded 'large', 'moderate-to-large', or 'bilateral large' in the report text and/or MeSH). Deliberately excludes small/trace/moderate effusions from expected_critical even when clearly documented -- several such cases (313, 576, 650, 1957, 2441, 2616, 3001) are included as negatives specifically to test that severity distinction, since only a LARGE pleural effusion is clinically critical, not any effusion.

Pneumomediastinum.note: IMPORTANT, MEASURED FACT, NOT A HYPOTHETICAL: only 7 of the 3955 probed reports mention pneumomediastinum (or MeSH's synonym 'Mediastinal Emphysema') at all. Of those 7: five are clean, unambiguous negations (studies 1705, 197, 2145, 3657, 3639, all in this gold set), one is a reference to patient history rather than a current-study finding (study 2467, in this gold set as a negative), and exactly ONE (study 895) has any affirmative signal at all -- and even that one is hedged ('less apparent', 'less perceptible'), classified positive here only on the strength of independent MeSH corroboration (Mediastinal Emphysema coded as a major finding). This gold set therefore has a SINGLE pneumomediastinum-positive case. This is not a gap I could close by looking harder in this corpus -- it is not padded with weak cases to hit a target count, and the label is NOT dropped from CRITICAL_LABELS despite the near-zero coverage, because it remains a clinically critical finding regardless of how rare confirmed examples are in OpenI. It also does NOT mean G1 is untestable for this label -- it means G1's pneumomediastinum coverage rests on exactly one hand-verified case, which is a materially weaker recall signal than the 14 cases each backing Pneumothorax and PleuralEffusion, and Phase 3's eval reporting should say so rather than present one unified recall number across all 3 labels as if they were equally well-tested.

metadata.reader_a_coverage_gap: medscope.readers.cnn.CNNReader (densenet121-res224-all) has 18 output pathologies including Pneumothorax and Effusion, but NOTHING for pneumomediastinum (confirmed at runtime via model.pathologies in Task 1.5). reader_a structurally cannot detect Pneumomediastinum at all -- recall on that label depends entirely on reader_b (the VLM), which does not exist until Phase 2. Any G1 run against reader_a alone can only ever be evaluated on Pneumothorax and PleuralEffusion; Pneumomediastinum recall is meaningless until reader_b lands.
metadata.image_availability: Deliberately not recorded here. It was, as `n_cases_with_local_image: 8` plus a per-case `image_available_locally` flag, and both became false the moment more of the 1.36 GB Open-i archive was fetched -- with nothing in the gate able to notice. medscope.eval resolves each case's `image_path` pattern against Settings.openi_root on every run and reports the measured count in its warnings instead.
known_heuristic_pitfalls_discovered: Negation scope: a fixed word-lookback window clips off negation triggers that appear at the start of a list of findings (e.g. 'Negative for consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax') -- fixed by scanning the whole sentence prefix instead.

Substring false-positives: 'large' matches inside 'larger' (a laterality comparison, not a severity grade) and inside 'enlarged' (usually describing the cardiac silhouette, not an effusion) -- fixed with word-boundary regex. See studies 313 and 1957.

'effusion' alone as a keyword also matches pericardial effusion, a distinct clinical entity from pleural effusion not covered by this ontology's PleuralEffusion label -- must be filtered out on manual read.

Corrupted/OCR-artifact negations (study 3085's 'Marrow pneumothorax' for what MeSH and the rest of the report make clear was almost certainly 'No pneumothorax') and mis-split sentence fragments (study 3170) defeat keyword+negation matching entirely and are only catchable by reading the full report and cross-checking MeSH.

'Resolved since prior exam' framing (studies 649, 2887) and 'history of' framing in INDICATION rather than a current FINDINGS assertion (study 2467) both mention a critical-label keyword prominently while describing a current negative.

cases.note: IMPRESSION: 'Recurrent right pneumothorax, complete collapse of the right lung, near 100%.' MeSH confirms Pneumothorax/right. Unambiguous large/complete pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION describes a hydropneumothorax (air+fluid in the pleural space) -- MeSH: Hydropneumothorax/right, Pleural Effusion/right. Counted as positive for both critical labels since hydropneumothorax is definitionally both processes at once; the effusion component isn't separately graded 'large' in the text, which is a judgment call, not a clean severity-graded case like the pure-effusion positives below.
IMPRESSION: 'Right-sided pneumothorax noted measuring approximately 1.8 cm from the right apex.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/apex/right. Measured, unambiguous.

IMPRESSION: 'Small 3.3 mm right-sided pneumothorax.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/right/small. Included despite 'small' because pneumothorax criticality (unlike pleural effusion) is not severity-gated in this design -- any confirmed pneumothorax is in CRITICAL_LABELS.

IMPRESSION: 'Large left hydropneumothorax, with complete collapse of the left lung.' MeSH: Hydropneumothorax/left/large -- the 'large' qualifier is explicit here (unlike study 1230), so both critical labels are confidently positive.
FINDINGS: 'thin right apical pneumothorax measuring approximately 5 mm.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/apex/right/small. Small but real and measured.
IMPRESSION: 'relatively large pneumothorax and collapse of substantial portion of left lung.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/left/large.
IMPRESSION: 'Stable 1 cm right apical pneumothorax.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/apex/right. 'Stable' means unchanged from a prior exam, not absent -- still a current positive finding.

IMPRESSION: 'Moderate right-sided hemopneumothorax.' MeSH: Hemopneumothorax/right/moderate, Pneumothorax/right/moderate. Hemopneumothorax = blood + air in the pleural space; counted as Pneumothorax only, not PleuralEffusion -- blood in the pleural space is hemothorax, a distinct entity from the simple/serous effusion 'PleuralEffusion' names in this ontology.
IMPRESSION: 'Large right pneumothorax with associated complete collapse of the right lower lobe.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/right/large.
IMPRESSION: 'Moderate right-sided pneumothorax measuring approximately 3.3 cm.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/apex/right/moderate.

IMPRESSION: 'Increased size of left pneumothorax... measures up to 3.5 cm.' Also has a small left pleural effusion/hemothorax (MeSH: Pleural Effusion/left/small) -- NOT counted as PleuralEffusion-critical since it's explicitly small, not large. Good multi-finding case: pneumothorax critical, coexisting small effusion is not.

IMPRESSION: 'Persistent 8mm pneumothorax with small amount of pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pneumothorax, Pleural Effusion/small. Same pattern as 3945 -- pneumothorax positive, coexisting effusion explicitly small so not critical.
IMPRESSION: 'Moderate sized right pneumothorax... measures 3.2 cm.' MeSH: Pneumothorax/apex/right/moderate.
IMPRESSION: 'Large left pleural effusion with minimal residual left lung aeration.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/left/large. (Report also notes a small right effusion -- not counted, not large.)
IMPRESSION: 'Bilateral large pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/bilateral/large.
IMPRESSION: 'Large right pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/right/large.
IMPRESSION: 'Moderate-to-large left pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/left/large. Explicit large-end grading despite the hedge phrasing ('moderate-to-large').

IMPRESSION: 'Interval development of large right-sided pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/right/large. Also explicitly negates pneumothorax in the same report ('There is no pneumothorax') -- good single-label-positive example.
IMPRESSION: 'Large right pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/right/large. Report also negates pneumothorax explicitly.

IMPRESSION: 'Patient is a large left effusion extending up to the level of the aortic [arch].' Grammatically garbled (likely dictation artifact) but MeSH confirms Pleural Effusion/left/large unambiguously.
IMPRESSION: 'Increasing large left pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/left/large. Also explicitly negates pneumothorax.
IMPRESSION: 'Large left lower lobe opacity represents a large layering pleural effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/left/large. Also explicitly negates pneumothorax.
IMPRESSION: 'Large right effusion.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/right/large.

IMPRESSION: 'bilateral pleural effusions' graded 'moderate to large' in FINDINGS, increasing from a prior exam. MeSH: Pleural Effusion/bilateral/large. Also explicitly negates pneumothorax. Report separately flags a possible pneumoperitoneum (free air below the diaphragm) -- irrelevant to chest critical labels, not counted.

IMPRESSION: 'Large right pleural effusion with associated passive atelectasis.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/right/large. Also explicitly negates pneumothorax ('No focal consolidation or pneumothorax identified').

The only case in the entire probed corpus (3955 reports) with any non-negated pneumomediastinum signal. FINDINGS text is genuinely hedged and reads almost self-contradictory: 'The right pneumothorax is not appreciated. Pneumomediastinum is also less perceptible.' -- 'not appreciated' reads like a negation in isolation. But IMPRESSION says 'The [prior] right pneumothorax and [prior] pneumomediastinum are less apparent' (comparative language: decreasing, not absent), and MeSH -- human-assigned, independent of the free-text negation this note is trying to resolve -- codes both as MAJOR findings: 'Pneumothorax/right' and 'Mediastinal Emphysema' (MeSH's own term for pneumomediastinum; added as an ontology alias for exactly this reason). INDICATION is literally 'Pneumo.', consistent with a known follow-up case. Classified positive on the strength of the MeSH corroboration, with this hedge fully documented since it is a genuine judgment call, not a clean-cut case.
Already committed at data/samples/studies/images/CXR38_IM-1911-1001.png (Task 1.2 sample). FINDINGS: 'no pneumothorax or pleural effusion.' MeSH: normal. Clean baseline negative.

Already committed at data/samples/studies/images/CXR797_IM-2332-1001.png (Task 1.2 sample, the cardiomegaly case used in the CNN slow test). FINDINGS explicitly negates pneumothorax and pleural effusion. Real positive finding here is Cardiomegaly, which is NOT a critical label -- good 'abnormal but not critical' example distinct from a normal study.

Already committed at data/samples/studies/images/CXR1187_IM-0126-1001.png (Task 1.2 sample, bilateral opacity case). FINDINGS: 'No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.' Real finding (bilateral airspace opacity) is unrelated to the 3 critical labels.
FINDINGS: 'No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.' MeSH: normal. Image locally available in the dev probe slice.
FINDINGS: "There's no pneumothorax." MeSH: normal. Image locally available.
FINDINGS: 'no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.' MeSH: Cardiomegaly/mild -- another 'real finding present, but not a critical one' case. Image locally available.

IMPRESSION: 'Does not appear to be a hydropneumothorax or empyema.' This is a negation my own build_critical_goldset.py heuristic initially MISSED (window-based lookback cut off 'negative for'-style triggers positioned earlier in a list; fixed to scan the whole sentence prefix -- see script comments). Real finding is a small right pleural effusion (MeSH: Pleural Effusion/right/small) -- not large, not critical. Also contains an unrelated hedge ('Cannot exclude a right lower lobe cavity') that has nothing to do with the 3 critical labels.

INDICATION is literally 'Right-sided pneumothorax' (prior known condition) and 'pneumothorax' appears prominently, but IMPRESSION says 'Previously identified small right pneumothorax is NOT visualized on today's exam' -- resolved since a prior study. MeSH does not code Pneumothorax at all, confirming the current study is negative. Exactly the kind of case a keyword-only extractor would misclassify as positive from the INDICATION field alone.

FINDINGS: 'Marrow pneumothorax, focal lung consolidation or pleural effusions.' 'Marrow' does not fit grammatically or clinically -- almost certainly OCR/transcription corruption of 'No pneumothorax, focal lung consolidation or pleural effusions.' Confirmed by IMPRESSION ('No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality') and MeSH ('No Indexing' -- no findings coded at all). Included specifically as a 'you will get bitten by this' example: a corrupted negation cue defeats keyword+negation matching entirely, and only reading the whole report plus MeSH catches it.

FINDINGS ends: '...Lungs are clear without evidence of fibrosis. Pleural effusions or pneumothorax. Endplate sclerotic changes...' -- an ungrammatical sentence fragment with no verb, almost certainly a mis-split continuation of the preceding negation ('without evidence of... pleural effusions or pneumothorax'). MeSH codes neither Pneumothorax nor Pleural Effusion, and IMPRESSION is clean ('No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality'). Confirms negative; another sentence-splitting/corruption pitfall.

FINDINGS: 'Evaluation for pneumothorax is limited due to exclusion of the superior-most pulmonary apices.' This is a technical-quality caveat, not an assertion of presence or absence -- MeSH corroborates ('Technical Quality of Image Unsatisfactory'), and the rest of the report and IMPRESSION ('No acute pulmonary disease') report nothing acute. Classified negative (no finding was actually reported), but the technical limitation is noted explicitly since 'no finding reported' is weaker ground truth than a clean negation elsewhere in this set.

FINDINGS: 'Cannot exclude elevation right hemidiaphragm... No evidence of pneumothorax.' The hedge ('cannot exclude') applies to hemidiaphragm elevation, NOT to any of the 3 critical labels -- pneumothorax is cleanly negated. Effusion is present (MeSH: Pleural Effusion/base/right) but with no size qualifier documented, so not counted as large/critical. Also mentions a separate pericardial effusion (MeSH: Pericardial Effusion) -- a distinct clinical entity from PleuralEffusion in this ontology, not counted.

FINDINGS: 'Cannot exclude early pulmonary edema... No visible pneumothorax.' The hedge is about pulmonary edema, not a critical label. Pneumothorax is cleanly negated; effusion is mentioned in a garbled fragment ('Two airspace consolidation or effusion') that MeSH does not corroborate (no Pleural Effusion MeSH term at all) -- likely another transcription artifact, treated as negative.
IMPRESSION: 'Cannot exclude small pleural effusions.' Textbook hedge language (matches the exact style flagged in the task spec), and explicitly 'small' even if present -- not critical either way.
IMPRESSION: 'Possible small right pleural effusion, without focal consolidation or pneumothorax.' Hedge ('possible') + explicitly small, and pneumothorax is negated in the same sentence.

IMPRESSION: 'Right pleural effusion with adjacent atelectasis.' A real, persistent effusion, but no size qualifier is ever given in FINDINGS, IMPRESSION, or MeSH (just 'Pleural Effusion/right', no size) -- not documented as large, so not counted as critical. Image locally available. Good example of 'real finding present, but severity insufficient for the critical gate.'

IMPRESSION: 'Moderate right-sided pleural effusion' (+ small left-sided). MeSH: Pleural Effusion/right/moderate, Pleural Effusion/left/small. 'Moderate' is explicitly below this gold set's 'large' bar for critical severity. Pneumothorax explicitly negated ('No pneumothorax'). Image locally available.

FINDINGS: 'The left apical pneumothorax has resolved.' IMPRESSION: 'resolution of small apical pneumothorax.' MeSH codes no Pneumothorax at all. A clean 'was present historically, resolved by the time of this study' case -- current study is negative despite 'pneumothorax' appearing twice.

FINDINGS: 'There are small pleural effusions, right larger than left.' This is a laterality comparison ('right LARGER than left'), not a severity grade -- and it caught a real bug in my own build_critical_goldset.py heuristic, which originally matched 'large' as a substring of 'larger' (and separately of 'enlarged') and misclassified this as large-severity. Fixed to use word-boundary regex matching. MeSH confirms: Pleural Effusion/bilateral/small -- genuinely small, not critical. Kept in the set specifically to document this pitfall.

Same 'larger than' substring trap as study 313: 'Bilateral pleural effusions, right larger than left.' MeSH: Pleural Effusion/left/small, Pleural Effusion/right/moderate -- moderate at most, not large, not critical.
FINDINGS: 'Negative for pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, or pleural effusion.' Clean list-negation covering all 3 critical labels in one sentence. MeSH: normal.

FINDINGS: 'No pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum.' MeSH does not code either. Clean negative for the two labels this report discusses (does not mention pleural effusion at all, so that label is simply absent from this report, not asserted negative).
FINDINGS: 'There is no pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum.' MeSH: normal. Clean negative.
FINDINGS: 'No pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum.' Clean negative; also explicitly negates effusion ('No effusion or infiltrate').

Both FINDINGS ('There is no evidence of pneumomediastinum or pneumothorax... There are no large pleural effusions') AND IMPRESSION ('No evidence of pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum') independently confirm all 3 critical labels negative -- the strongest double-confirmation negative in the set, and notably the ONE report in the whole corpus that explicitly qualifies effusion size ('no LARGE pleural effusions') the same way this gold set does.

INDICATION: 'History of recent pneumomediastinum.' This is patient history, not a finding on THIS study -- FINDINGS for this exam describes unrelated small lung nodules and does not re-affirm or re-examine the mediastinum for pneumomediastinum at all. Classified negative for this study (no current finding reported), while flagging that this is exactly the kind of report where a keyword-only extractor would wrongly fire on the word 'pneumomediastinum' appearing prominently in INDICATION.
